inspiration.observed_pattern: A multi-table UPDATE LEFT JOINs a reference table, then fills snapshot fields from the most recent effective child price selected by a correlated scalar subquery with ORDER BY and LIMIT, falling back through joined defaults.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an original order-line catalog: an UPDATE JOIN chooses the latest active purchase price at or before each order date, using purchase_id to break same-date ties, then COALESCE falls back to the catalog default and finally zero. A second correlated scalar lookup drives an explicit source label, while cancelled rows remain unchanged.

fixture_notes: Order 11 selects the higher purchase_id among two prices on the same date; order 12 selects the latest active price; order 13 falls back to the catalog default; order 14 has neither source and falls back to zero; cancelled order 15 is excluded and retains its sentinel values.
determinism_notes: All product, price, and order identifiers and dates are fixed; the correlated price lookup orders by effective date and unique price ID, and final reads use primary-key order. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE catalog (product_id INT PRIMARY KEY, default_cost DECIMAL(10,2) NULL)
CREATE TABLE purchase_prices (price_id INT PRIMARY KEY, product_id INT NOT NULL, effective_on DATE NOT NULL, unit_cost DECIMAL(10,2) NULL, active TINYINT NOT NULL)

CREATE TABLE order_lines (line_id INT PRIMARY KEY, product_id INT NOT NULL, ordered_on DATE NOT NULL, quantity INT NOT NULL, cost_unit DECIMAL(10,2) NULL, cost_source VARCHAR(16) NULL, cancelled TINYINT NOT NULL)

steps.sql: UPDATE order_lines ol LEFT JOIN catalog c ON c.product_id = ol.product_id SET ol.cost_unit = COALESCE((SELECT p.unit_cost FROM purchase_prices p WHERE p.product_id = ol.product_id AND p.active = 1 AND p.effective_on <= ol.ordered_on ORDER BY p.effective_on DESC, p.price_id DESC LIMIT 1), c.default_cost, 0), ol.cost_source = CASE WHEN (SELECT p.unit_cost FROM purchase_prices p WHERE p.product_id = ol.product_id AND p.active = 1 AND p.effective_on <= ol.ordered_on ORDER BY p.effective_on DESC, p.price_id DESC LIMIT 1) IS NOT NULL THEN 'purchase' WHEN c.default_cost IS NOT NULL THEN 'catalog' ELSE 'zero' END WHERE ol.cancelled = 0

checks.sql: SELECT line_id, product_id, ordered_on, quantity, cost_unit, cost_source, cancelled FROM order_lines ORDER BY line_id
SELECT price_id, product_id, effective_on, unit_cost, active FROM purchase_prices ORDER BY price_id
